data_objects.name: passenger_manifest
data_objects.meaning: Passenger-level manifest records containing travel class, identity, family-companion counts, ticketing, cabin, embarkation, fare, age, and sex attributes.
data_objects.notes: Blank cells represent unavailable age, fare, cabin, or other manifest attributes.

variables.name: Pclass
variables.meaning: Ordinal passenger-class code, with class numbers encoded as integers.

variables.name: Name
variables.meaning: Passenger name, often including title and parenthetical alternate or spouse-related name text.

variables.name: Sex
variables.meaning: Passenger sex category recorded as text.

variables.name: Age
variables.meaning: Passenger age; fractional values can represent ages below or between whole years.

variables.name: SibSp
variables.meaning: Number of siblings and spouses accompanying the passenger.

variables.name: Parch
variables.meaning: Number of parents and children accompanying the passenger.

variables.name: Ticket
variables.meaning: Ticket identifier or ticket-code string; it can be shared by multiple passengers.

variables.name: Fare
variables.meaning: Passenger fare amount in an unspecified currency.

variables.name: Cabin
variables.meaning: Cabin assignment text; a cell can contain more than one cabin code.

variables.name: Embarked
variables.meaning: Embarkation-port category encoded by a one-letter code.

structure.description: Each row represents one passenger, and PassengerId is the passenger-record key and ascending row-order field.
Ticket and Cabin can group or relate passengers but are not passenger identifiers; Pclass is an ordinal categorical field.

uncertainties: The CSV does not map the Embarked letters to named ports.
The fare currency and any rules governing shared ticket fares or multiple-cabin strings are not documented.
annotation_notes: Only the declared train.csv and its neutral packet were used as evidence.
